introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, answer all questions): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Figure 11* shows a light signal entering into an optical fibre.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_9_fig_1.png)

A pulse of light is emitted by switching on the source for $1.0\ \mu\mathrm{s}$. The light is emitted in many directions as shown. The critical angle at the core/cladding boundary is $59^\circ$ and the length of the fibre is $6.0\ \mathrm{km}$. The refractive index of the core is $1.50$.

(i) State two advantages that optical fibres have over copper cables in telecommunication.

(ii) Some light from the source will travel straight down the fibre for its entire length. Determine how long it takes to travel the entire length of the fibre.

(iii) What is the refractive index of the cladding? *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two advantages** (any two): an optical fibre has a much **larger bandwidth** (carries far more information, many more channels at once); the signal suffers **less attenuation** (fewer repeaters needed); it is **immune to electromagnetic interference** and there is no cross-talk between fibres; it is **more secure** (hard to tap), **lighter, thinner and cheaper** per unit of information (silica instead of copper).

**(ii) Travel time along the axis.** Speed of light in the core: $v = \dfrac{c}{n} = \dfrac{3.00\times10^{8}}{1.50} = 2.00\times10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Distance $L = 6.0\ \mathrm{km} = 6.0\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{m}$:
$$t = \frac{L}{v} = \frac{6.0\times10^{3}}{2.00\times10^{8}} = 3.0\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{s}$$
**$t = 3.0\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{s} = 30\ \mu\mathrm{s}$.**

**(iii) Refractive index of the cladding.** At the critical angle $C$, the refracted ray travels along the boundary ($90^\circ$): $n_{\text{core}}\sin C = n_{\text{cladding}}\sin90^\circ$, so
$$n_{\text{cladding}} = n_{\text{core}}\sin C = 1.50\times\sin59^\circ = 1.50\times0.857 = 1.29$$
**$n_{\text{cladding}} \approx 1.29$.** (It is lower than the core index, as required for total internal reflection.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Figure 12* shows the block diagram of a simple radio transmitter.

![fig-2](gce-al-physics-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_9_fig_2.png)

(i) State the function of the microphone and the modulator.

(ii) Briefly explain the difference between amplitude modulation (A.M.) and frequency modulation (F.M.).

(iii) State one advantage that each of F.M. and A.M. has over the other. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Functions.**

- The **microphone** converts sound (pressure variations) into an **electrical signal** (the audio frequency signal) with the same pattern and frequency.
- The **modulator** combines the audio signal with the high-frequency **carrier wave** from the oscillator, so that either the amplitude or the frequency of the carrier varies in step with the audio signal. The result is passed to the radio frequency amplifier and the aerial.

**(ii) A.M. and F.M.**

- In **amplitude modulation**, the **amplitude** of the carrier varies in proportion to the amplitude of the audio signal, while the carrier **frequency stays constant**.
- In **frequency modulation**, the **frequency** of the carrier varies in proportion to the amplitude of the audio signal (the rate of variation follows the audio frequency), while the carrier **amplitude stays constant**.

**(iii) One advantage of each.**

- F.M. over A.M.: F.M. is **less affected by noise and interference** (noise mostly changes amplitude, which the receiver ignores), giving better quality (higher fidelity) reception.
- A.M. over F.M.: A.M. needs a **smaller bandwidth** (so more stations can share the band), has a **greater range** (long and medium waves are reflected by the ionosphere or follow the ground), and the transmitters and receivers are simpler and cheaper.

questions.enonce_markdown: State three advantages of digital transmission over analogue transmission. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any three:

- **Less noise and distortion**: a digital signal (only two levels) can be **regenerated** exactly by repeaters, so noise does not accumulate; an analogue signal is amplified together with its noise.
- **Error detection and correction** are possible, so the received information is more accurate.
- A larger number of signals can share the same channel (**multiplexing**), so the **capacity is greater**.
- Speech, text, images and video are all sent in the **same form**, so the signals are easily processed, stored and switched by computers.
- Digital signals are easier to **encrypt**, hence more secure, and the circuits are cheaper and more reliable.
